newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dlr, stg vols ease amid seesawing spot.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr, stg vols ease amid seesawing spot.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar and sterling options were steady to easier across the board, with choppy moves in spot rates discouraging trade in volatilities, traders said.

"The dollar seems to have finished its assault against the mark for now, but the market sees it as a correction and not a real downward trend. So because of this, volatilities are weakening, mainly at the short-end," said Yoshiaki Yamamoto, an options trader at Sakura Bank in London.
One-month dollar/mark vols were quoted at 11.00/30 percent at 1125 GMT, unchanged from levels seen in late European trade on Wednesday.
But risk reversals, the differential between put and call pricing, showed demand for dollar calls was easing as dollar-bull sentiment was flagging, at least in the short term.
Dollar/mark 25-delta risk reversals backed down to around par from 0.3/0.6 in favour of dollar calls on Wednesday.
"For the time being there's the speculation about higher German interest rates, and this is making the risk reversal close to flat," Sakura's Yamamoto said.

Spot dollar/mark, after falling by nearly four pfennings on Wednesday, had been seesawing between 1.83 and 1.84 marks for most of Europe's morning session. It was at 1.8354/64 at 1135 GMT, almost unchanged from its late Wednesday European level.
Dollar/yen vols also eased as the spot rate appeared to have established a foothold above 115 yen for now, traders said.

One-month vols were quoted at 10.60/90 percent against late Wednesday's 11.10/40, while spot dollar yen was at 116.44/54 against 115.65/75. Risk reversals still favoured dollar puts at 0.1/0.4 against 0.0/0.3.

Concerning volatilities in sterling/mark options, traders said that although their vols were high compared to those of other major currency pairs, they appeared to be cooling off while spot sterling/mark tries to establish a base after recent fluctuations.
However, they added that the market was still nervous because of sterling/mark's sharp moves -- most of them downwards -- since the beginning of the month.

"It's a bit tricky with sterling. Some people are starting to think that perhaps we've had our bull run, and there's all this talk about a delay in EMU as well (which is helping that mark), so they are less bullish than they used to be," said a trader at a U.S. bank here.
One-month sterling/mark vols were at 12.30/70 percent against Wednesday's 12.50/13.00. Demand remained biased towards sterling puts with risk reversals at 0.5/1.0 against 0.3/0.8.

Mark/yen vols backed down as well as the German currency climbed off the 25-month lows it set earlier this week. One-month was quoted at 10.80/30 against 11.10/40, while spot was at 63.42/45 against 63.02/05, well above the 25-month low of 62.05 set on Monday.
